chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, "Can the earth remain without an Imam?" He said, "No." I said, "We narrate that it does not remain except when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, becomes wrathful with the servants." He said, "It does not remain; otherwise, it would sink."

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: an Imam, the divinely appointed guide and authority
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the earth, understood here as the inhabited world requiring Divine Authority
key_terms.يَسْخَطَ: to be wrathful; referring to Allah’s anger toward the servants

ai.seo_question: Can the earth remain without an Imam according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the earth cannot remain without an Imam, indicating the perpetual necessity of a Divine Authority among creation. It presents the Imam as essential to the order and preservation of the world, and thus reflects a foundational teaching concerning Imamate in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Would the earth remain without an Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘We are reporting that it would not remain except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Bog it down upon the servants’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would not remain except it would bog down (its inhabitants)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Ali has narrated from Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ who has said the following.

“I asked al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.), “I can the earth remain without Imam?” The Imam (a.s.) replied, “No, it will not remain so.” I said, “We narrate that it will not remain without the Imam unless Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, becomes angry with the people.” The Imam said, “In such condition it will not remain but it will obliterate its inhabitants.”
